title: Risk Governance & Thematic Review Panels
summary: Prepares supervisory staff to participate effectively in risk governance panels (RGPs) and thematic review panels (TRPs) — internal governance mechanisms used to review and challenge supervisory assessments and thematic findings.
contentGaps: deliveryFormat: not stated in source catalogue; defaulted to In-person pending confirmation
intendedAudience: generic per-track guidance, not individually sourced
priorKnowledge: inferred from course title/track, not stated in source

sections.Aim and Purpose: Prepares supervisory staff to participate effectively in risk governance panels (RGPs) and thematic review panels (TRPs) — internal governance mechanisms used to review and challenge supervisory assessments and thematic findings.
sections.Intended Audience: Junior to mid-level supervisory staff conducting day-to-day risk assessment and firm engagement.
sections.Learning Objectives:
- Explain the role and purpose of thematic review panels and risk governance panels
- Describe the operating procedures for both panel types, including the role of key participants
- Identify the main components of the RGP and TRP report
- Explain the do's and don'ts for panel members and presenters
- Discuss the importance of challenging and open discussion in panels
sections.Syllabus:
**Morning | 09:30–13:00** — What are risk governance and thematic review panels? Purpose and types of panel within the overall supervisory risk framework, including lessons from risk assurance reviews Thematic review panels: what drives thematic reviews, types of review, how to set one up effectively, avoiding the ‘Christmas tree effect’ of over-scoping Managing moral hazard from thematic reviews; thematic governance panel composition, packs, role and reporting Risk governance panels: purpose, frequency, duration, composition, and how RGPs support supervisors

**Afternoon | 14:00–16:00** — Panel operation, roles and case study The phases of an RGP: pre-panel meeting, panel discussion (preliminary issues, core issues, conclusions), post-panel actions and follow-up Selecting and preparing panel members; role of presenters, panel chair, and panel secretary; meeting minutes and observer etiquette Preparing an RGP pack: key content, supervisory narrative, supporting information, assessing materiality Case study: a firm risk assessment exercise applying the panel process end-to-end
sections.Structure and Format:
Delivered as a single full-day workshop.

> **Content gap:** delivery channel (in-person/online/hybrid) was not specified in the source catalogue and defaults to In-person pending confirmation.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with ongoing supervision is helpful but not essential.
